sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Context**: The Kheda district faced severe drought and plague, leading to a massive failure of the Kharif crop. 
• **Legal Provision**: The **Revenue Code** stipulated that if the yield was less than 25% of the normal produce, farmers were entitled to a full remission of land revenue. 
• **Government Stance**: The British administration rejected the peasants' plea for remission and insisted on full collection, using coercive measures like confiscation of property. 
• **Key Metric**: The **'No-Tax' Campaign** was the primary mechanism, where peasants were urged to withhold revenue as a form of non-violent resistance.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Mass Mobilization**: Use of vernacular language and local networks to reach the rural masses.
• **Non-Violent Resistance**: Strict adherence to 'Ahimsa' despite government provocation and property seizure.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Internal divisions among the peasantry and the threat of land confiscation.
• **Solutions**: Gandhi's insistence on 'voluntary suffering' to build moral pressure on the colonial state.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'C-A-K' (Chronological order of Gandhi's early movements).
• **Decoded Meaning**: C (Champaran 1917) -> A (Ahmedabad 1918) -> K (Kheda 1918).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses Kheda with Champaran. Remember: Champaran was about Indigo (Plantation/Contractual), Kheda was about Land Revenue (Drought/Natural Calamity).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Peasant-Nationalist Synergy' to describe how local agrarian issues were integrated into the broader national struggle.

keyTakeaways: Kheda was the first instance of a 'No-Tax' campaign in the Indian freedom struggle.
It established the 'Patidar' community as a major political force in Gujarat.
The movement proved that the British government could be forced to negotiate through organized, non-violent mass pressure.
